study: Prast et al. 2018 — project GROW differentiated-instruction math PD, Dutch cluster RCT, primary grades 1-6, Learning and Instruction 54:22-34
delivery_evidence: 2-year GROW PD delivered face-to-face: ten 3-hour team meetings per school year (teachers learned the differentiation cycle, collectively prepared/videotaped/evaluated lessons via Lesson Study), school-based project coaches trained in five regional in-person meetings, plus classroom observations; principals present at team meetings (Sec. 2.5/2.5.2, p.~26-27).
test_alignment_evidence: Outcome is the Cito Mathematics Tests (CMT), the national Dutch curriculum-based progress-monitoring battery (vertically-scaled competence score) — a broad standardized instrument not tailored to the GROW differentiation PD (extraction test_type=standardized_independent; Sec. 2.4/Tables 5&7).
curriculum_evidence: GROW teaches teachers to apply the cycle of differentiation (flexible within-class ability grouping, differentiated instruction) in their existing primary-mathematics teaching; no new math curriculum or materials package is adopted — control is business-as-usual math (Intro/Sec. 2.5, p.~24-26).
outcome_timing_evidence: Extracted effect sizes are the PD effect on the within-year math-achievement growth slope measured at the end of the active intervention year (Cohort 1 end-Year-1; Cohort 2 end-Year-2) — immediate post; the n.s. Year-2 follow-up of Year-1 PD was not the extracted wave (Tables 5&7; extraction timepoint=end-of-year post).
